tagline: Run trustworthy online experiments, including tests of AI features, and defend a launch, iterate or stop decision with the right interval
description: Participants run the statistics behind an experimentation programme that includes tests of AI features. On a synthetic event stream from Sufrah, a fictional food-delivery marketplace, they check tests for trust problems, analyse triggered exposure, reduce variance with pre-experiment data, compute intervals for ratio metrics, design sequential tests for daily monitoring, set guardrails for latency, cost and harm, and measure interference through shared couriers, ending on a mock review board that decides launch, iterate or stop.
audience: Specialists. Analysts and data scientists who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: an analysis or model they built, validated and can explain.
prerequisites: Writes SQL with joins and window functions over event logs
Pre-work: two hours on power and the two-sample test, with an entry quiz (see labs/README.md)
Setup: a laptop processor with uv, or Google Colab. No lab calls a model or downloads one. Run 00_setup_check before Day 1.

outcomes.text: Apply regression adjustment with pre-experiment data and report the sample-size saving, given a test with 28 days of pre-period data per customer
outcomes.evidence: unadjusted and adjusted intervals with the effective sample-size gain

outcomes.text: Compute intervals for ratio metrics with the delta method and with a bootstrap over the randomisation unit, given order-level logs from a customer-randomised test
outcomes.evidence: two agreeing intervals and a note on why the naive one is too narrow

outcomes.text: Implement group sequential and always-valid tests and measure their false-positive rates under daily monitoring by simulation, given a simulator with and without a true effect
outcomes.evidence: error rates at or below the nominal level, with expected stopping times

outcomes.text: Design the metric set, power and decision rule for launching an AI feature, given a proposed AI-ranked search change with goals and expected traffic
outcomes.evidence: a pre-registration with guardrail thresholds, sample size and a written decision rule

outcomes.text: Diagnose interference in a marketplace test and design a cluster or switchback alternative with its power, given a simulator in which treated customers take couriers from control customers
outcomes.evidence: a memo quantifying the naive bias and the power of the new design

outcomes.text: Review experiment write-ups and decide launch, iterate or stop for each, given five write-ups with seeded faults such as sample ratio mismatch, peeking and novelty decay
outcomes.evidence: a review log scored against reference decisions

case_study.name: Sufrah
case_study.summary: Sufrah is a fictional food-delivery marketplace in six Saudi cities whose experimentation programme now tests AI features: AI-ranked search and Luqma, an in-app chat assistant. Participants check its tests for trust problems, size and analyse the AI-ranked search test with variance reduction and ratio intervals, monitor tests daily without inflating false wins, measure how a dispatch test is biased by shared couriers, and sit on its review board. All data is synthetic and generated with fixed seeds: 200,000 customers, about two million orders, a daily-peeking simulator and a marketplace simulator.

format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
